plan.summary: A standard-mode, 12-month plan for MSFT as of 2026-09-19, revised after review. Evidence base: the FY2026 10-K (year ended June 2026), the FY2025 and FY2024 10-Ks, FY2026 10-Qs, 8-K earnings releases, the 2026 proxy and regulator dockets. Question 1 is tested on the PP&E and useful-life notes plus the forward-cost disclosures that pre-announce future charges: leases signed but not yet commenced, and purchase and construction commitments. Question 2 becomes two steps: construct the multiple from filed earnings and cash flow against the as-of close, place it against its own trailing series and against peers, then run a reverse DCF that solves one variable at a time with the other three held at stated, sourced values printed beside each result. Question 3 asks not only where AI revenue is separately disclosed but whether seat growth can be separated from per-seat price and whether product lines were reclassified; partner economics below operating income (equity-method, other income, related-party) are examined separately. No figure appears in this plan; every number is computed downstream by the engine from fetched filings.

challenges.statement: Operator question 2 asks what must be true for the current multiple to be justified, but no section establishes or contextualises the multiple itself. The plan jumps straight to a reverse DCF, whose implied growth/margin/discount path is uninterpretable without a reference point: where the multiple sits against its own multi-year history, against the peers already being pulled for useful lives, and against the growth path the market is publicly assumed to expect.
challenges.suggestion: Add to valuation_dcf an explicit multiple construction from filed earnings/cash flow and the as-of price, plus a trailing multiple series from the planned market-data source, and state whether the reverse-DCF implied path is above or below the peer-disclosed growth already in hand.

challenges.statement: The reverse DCF is described as solving simultaneously for revenue growth path, steady-state margin, capex-to-revenue and discount rate from a single observed price. One price cannot identify four unknowns; every reported 'implied condition' is in fact conditional on three others being fixed by the engine. The named risk covers horizon/fade/reinvestment assumptions but not this identification problem, which could make the section's headline output look like a derived fact.
challenges.suggestion: Require the section to solve for one variable at a time with the others held at stated, sourced values, and to report the held values alongside each solved figure; name underdetermination as an explicit plan risk.

challenges.statement: growth_outlook plans to locate AI-attributable revenue disclosures, but never asks the reclassification question the investment_thesis promises to answer. If AI monetisation arrives largely as price uplift on existing bundled suites or as seat-level attach rather than a separate line, no disaggregation will reveal it, and 'newly disclosed AI revenue' will be confused with repriced legacy revenue.
challenges.suggestion: Add a focus asking whether FY2024-FY2026 disclosures let seat growth be separated from per-seat pricing in the relevant product lines, and whether any product reclassification between lines occurred; if not, record it as the bound on question 3.

challenges.statement: Nothing in the plan addresses non-operating items tied to AI partnerships: equity-method income or loss, funding or investment commitments to model partners, and any related-party revenue arising from those arrangements. These sit below segment operating income, so both earnings_quality and segment_analysis would miss them, yet they bear directly on reported earnings feeding the multiple and on whether AI revenue is arm's-length third-party demand.
challenges.suggestion: Add to earnings_quality or cash_flow_analysis a focus on the equity-method investment note, other income/expense detail, and related-party disclosure in the FY2026 10-K and proxy, stating whether partner-related revenue is disclosed or unresolvable.

challenges.statement: Question 1 turns on future depreciation and lease charges, but no section names the two disclosures that pre-announce them: leases signed but not yet commenced, and third-party capacity purchase commitments. The commitments note is planned only inside capital_allocation, framed as a buyback-versus-capex trade-off, not as embedded future cost that will land in cloud cost of revenue after the 12-month horizon begins.
challenges.suggestion: Route the leases note (including not-yet-commenced leases) and the purchase/construction commitments note into earnings_quality as forward cost evidence, and into scenarios_sensitivities as the basis for the depreciation step-up axis.

challenges.statement: Stock-based compensation is absent from every section focus. It is a recurring charge inside the segment margins whose durability is being tested, and the reverse DCF takes a point-in-time diluted share count while capital_allocation looks at buybacks without netting dilution. A margin trend partly driven by SBC as a share of revenue would be invisible to the plan as written.
challenges.suggestion: Add SBC as a line item in earnings_quality's three-year margin bridge, and require valuation_dcf to state how SBC and net share count change are treated in the implied-conditions solve.

critique.coverage_note: Attacked the plan only, on coverage, sources and method; no view on the company is expressed or implied. The evidence hierarchy, the non-GAAP-versus-audited separation, and the labelling of transcript figures are genuine strengths and I found nothing wrong with them. Challenges cluster on question 2's framing and on cost and income items that fall outside the segment-margin lens the plan uses.

sections.focus: Operator question 1, in two halves. Reported: PP&E and depreciation policy, any change in estimated useful lives for server and network equipment, capitalised versus expensed infrastructure and capitalised software in the FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024 10-Ks, read against capex, depreciation and segment operating income. Committed: the leases note including leases signed but not yet commenced, and the fiscal 2026 purchase and construction commitments note, as cost that enters cloud cost of revenue during or after the horizon. State what the disclosure cannot attribute rather than inferring it.

Segment revenue and operating income for each reportable segment from the FY2026 10-K segment note with FY2025 and FY2024 comparatives, plus revenue disaggregation by product and service line. Check whether segment composition or line definitions were restated and whether multi-year comparison survives it. Separate the company-level Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage, a non-GAAP measure in the earnings release, from audited segment operating margin, and say which of the two the durability question can actually be tested on.

Operator question 2, two steps. (1) Construct the multiple: filed FY2026 earnings, diluted shares and free cash flow against the 2026-09-19 close, plus a trailing multiple series built from the market-data price history and the FY2024-FY2026 filed series, and peer multiples built the same way. (2) Reverse DCF solved for one variable at a time - revenue growth path, steady-state margin, capex-to-revenue, discount rate - with the other three held at stated, sourced values printed beside each solved figure, plus the terminal-value share. Output is conditions implied by the price under stated holds, not a fair value.

Operator question 3, disclosure side. Locate every AI-attributable revenue disclosure in the FY2024-FY2026 filings and earnings releases: named lines in the revenue disaggregation, any quantified contribution to Azure growth, remaining performance obligations and their expected recognition window, and unearned revenue movement. Where AI revenue is not separately reported, say so and bound the question by what is disclosed rather than estimating. Transcript commentary is carried as a labelled assertion, never as a measured figure.

Operator question 3, composition side, plus the base series the multiple uses. Across the FY2024-FY2026 10-Ks and 10-Qs, track whether product and service lines were renamed, merged or reclassified, and whether any disclosure lets seat or user growth be separated from per-seat price in the affected suites. If price uplift on existing bundles cannot be distinguished from new AI demand, record that as the bound on question 3. Assemble the three-year revenue, operating income, diluted EPS and free cash flow series used in multiple construction.

Stress the implied conditions along the axes the operator's questions raise: a depreciation step-up sized from the not-yet-commenced leases and purchase and construction commitments identified in earnings_quality; an AI revenue ramp delayed one and two years; a higher required return; a capex plateau with utilisation improving. Each run varies one input from the stated base hold set; combination runs print every changed value. All figures computed by the engine from filed inputs.

Three years of operating, investing and financing cash flow from the FY2026 10-K plus FY2026 10-Q quarterly detail. Trace cash capex and finance-lease capacity additions against operating cash flow. Then the layer below segment income: equity-method income or loss and its cash-flow reconciliation, other income and expense detail, investment or funding outflows to AI model partners, and related-party revenue disclosed in the 10-K or proxy, stating for each whether partner-linked amounts are disclosed or unresolvable. Also buybacks, dividends, debt issued and repaid, and the maturity schedule.

External benchmarks for questions 1 and 2. From the latest Amazon and Alphabet 10-Ks: disclosed server and infrastructure useful lives and any estimate change, capex, depreciation and cloud segment operating income, so Microsoft's capitalisation policy can be placed as usual or unusual. From those filings plus market data, peer multiples constructed on the same basis at the as-of date. Third-party consensus growth expectations, if obtainable, are reported as labelled estimates and never as evidence about the company.

Risks sourced to the FY2026 10-K Item 1A, the contingencies note and named proceedings on official regulator dockets. Prioritise: committed depreciation and lease charges outrunning cloud demand; customer and funded-partner concentration the filings do not disaggregate; antitrust and cloud-licensing remedies; AI model liability and emerging regulation; macro demand against a cost base fixed in advance. Each risk names the disclosure it rests on and whether it is sized or unsized in the filings.

Dated events inside the 12-month horizon: FY2027 quarterly earnings dates announced by the company, the annual meeting date from the 2026 proxy, debt maturities from the 10-K schedule, any disclosed commencement dates for signed-but-not-commenced leases, and regulator-published decision or deadline dates on open proceedings. Only events with a source-stated date or a disclosed expected window are listed; undated expectations are marked as such.

themes.label: AI infrastructure capital expenditure buildout
themes.rationale: Microsoft's massive data center and GPU capex to expand Azure AI capacity is a direct exposure to this theme; capex intensity and depreciation drag on margins are material to earnings and cash flow.

themes.label: Enterprise cloud migration and infrastructure spend
themes.rationale: Azure is a core growth engine riding continued enterprise migration off on-prem infrastructure; Azure growth rate is a primary metric investors track for Microsoft's overall revenue trajectory.

themes.label: Generative AI product monetization
themes.rationale: Copilot integration across Microsoft 365, GitHub, and Azure AI services represents the company's attempt to convert AI investment into per-seat and consumption revenue, a key thesis driver for the stock.

themes.label: Grid electrification and power constraints
themes.rationale: Microsoft's data center buildout is increasingly power-constrained, pushing it into nuclear, gas, and renewable power purchase agreements; grid capacity availability directly gates its AI capacity expansion timeline.

assumptions.justification: The mean of capital expenditure over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.1205, 0.1326, 0.1814, 0.2291, 0.3494.

assumptions.justification: The mean of operating income over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.4206, 0.4177, 0.4464, 0.4562, 0.4678.

assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: Anchored to the company's own derived economics rather than to trading comparables. EBIT margin 44.2% plus D&A intensity 8.7% implies EBITDA near 53% of revenue; at a 17.5% tax rate and terminal capex reverting to roughly the depreciation level, free cash conversion of EBITDA is near two-thirds, which against a ~8-9% discount rate and 3.0% perpetual growth supports roughly 12-14x. I set 14x at the upper end for franchise durability. The risk is capex: intensity ran 34.9% of revenue in FY2026 and finance-lease interest nearly doubled, so if the buildout does not normalize, conversion falls and 10-11x is fairer. Of the two, I regard the 3.0% perpetuity as the better terminal estimate, because it is built from the derived cash flows; this multiple is a cross-check on it.

assumptions.name: revenue_growth
assumptions.justification: The compound annual growth rate of revenue from 2022-06-30 to 2026-06-30, over 4 year(s): revenue moved from 198,270,000,000 to 331,839,000,000. Held flat across the forecast, because a trailing rate is one number and projecting a fade is a judgement this derivation does not make.

assumptions.name: risk_free_rate
assumptions.justification: The US 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield was 4.94% on 2026-09-17, as published by 2026-09-19 (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), series DGS10). Taken as the USD risk-free rate for this run's as-of date and converted to the fraction 0.0494.

assumptions.name: tax_rate
assumptions.justification: The mean of income tax expense over pre tax income across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.1311, 0.1898, 0.1823, 0.1763, 0.1940.

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.justification: Taken as below a discount rate of at least 7% — with the 4.94% risk-free from the filings-derived set, any ordinary equity cost for MSFT sits well above that, so 3.0% is safely below the WACC eventually confirmed. It rests on the view that a perpetual rate cannot exceed long-run nominal GDP; 3.0% places Microsoft at roughly economy-level growth with a small premium for a cloud/productivity franchise the research describes as one of two scale leaders. The 13.7% trailing CAGR is a forecast-period input, not evidence for perpetuity. I would lower it toward 2.0-2.5% if the terminal state is judged to be a slower-growing, capex-heavy infrastructure business rather than a software one, and raise it toward 3.5% only with evidence that AI demand durably lifts the category's long-run nominal growth. Note this is partly convention: no filing supports a perpetual rate.

assumptions.name: working_capital_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of net working capital — current assets less current liabilities — over revenue, across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. A negative figure is normal for a business paid before it pays, and is proposed as it stands rather than floored at zero.

The two terminal methods disagree by more than a quarter. That is information, not an error: they are two different guesses about the same unknowable quantity, and the distance between them is the honest width of the answer.

The bridge from enterprise value to equity value is net debt alone. Associate holdings, minority interests and pension deficits are not read off the filings by this build, so a business carrying material non-operating items is valued as though it does not.
